Subject: Post-demo: initial questions on auth, rotation, and sandbox access

Rafael / Marissa / Ben,

Appreciate the deep dive today — the demo helped a lot. Two quick notes from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope engineering work: 

1) High-level preference: LedgerWorks would like to avoid long-lived static API keys in production for security/controls reasons. We'd prefer either short-lived JWTs issued by our IdP (we use Okta) that Redwood will validate, or Redwood-managed service accounts that rotate automatically.

2) Rotation window: our security team requires key rotation at least every 90 days for any long-lived secret. Short-lived tokens (<1 hour) are preferred for any production traffic.

3) Sandbox access: we need a simple SDK bootstrap so devs can try embeddings + rerank locally. Ideally that uses ephemeral tokens tied to our sandbox workspace. Can you outline options and a rough delivery timeline?

4) Compliance evidence: please share any SOC2 / pen test artifacts you can for procurement review (we can accept redacted versions). I've attached a high-level requirements_summary.pdf so you can see the procurement checklist.

Next steps from us: confirm whether Redwood recommends (A) service-account-based JWTs validated by Redwood using our IdP, (B) Redwood-issued ephemeral tokens backed by our signed assertion, or (C) per-service API keys with rotation via KMS. Also confirm SDK changes required for structured outputs/tool-calling and how you'd secure those RPCs.

Thanks — I can free up time for a technical follow-up next Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

— Sanjay Rao

Sanjay — thanks for the clear notes and for the attachment. Quick summary / our recommended approach and proposed next steps below.

TL;DR recommendation: service-account JWTs for production + Redwood-issued short-lived sandbox tokens for developer onboarding. This balances auditability + low ops friction.

Why service-account JWTs (prod):
- Better for audit logs and identity mapping (we can emit per-service principal traces).
- Works with your Okta IdP via OIDC federation; tokens can be short-lived (1h) and validated via JWKS.
- Key rotation handled by customer KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations) or Redwood-managed rotation if you prefer us to hold the private key.

Sandbox/dev UX: Redwood can issue ephemeral tokens scoped to a sandbox workspace (TTL 1h-24h) — those are minted by Redwood's control plane after a short OIDC handshake or an API call authenticated by a short-lived assertion. That makes the SDK bootstrap trivial: devs exchange a developer assertion for a token, then call the SDK.

Auth flow options (summary):
A) Customer-managed service account (recommended for prod) — you sign JWTs with your KMS; we verify.
B) Redwood-managed service account — we rotate keys on your behalf; we can surface rotation events to your audit log.
C) Static API keys (not recommended) — easier, but fails your rotation requirement unless automated via a vault.

SDK implications:
- Minimal changes for token handling: the SDK will accept either an API key header (x-api-key) or a Bearer token.
- We'll add a helper for the OIDC exchange (30–60 LOC) and a sample for embedding/rerank sequences and structured tool-calls.
- For tool-calling we recommend signed callbacks (HMAC) or mutual TLS for high-sensitivity endpoints; we can configure RBAC per route.

Attachments I pushed into the thread: redwood-auth-diagram-v1.png (simple flow).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (1 hour) — Marissa to lead. Proposed slots: Tue 09/21 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 09/22 13:00–14:00 PT.
2) We'll produce a one-page runbook outlining the OIDC assertions and sample SDK code (editable Google Doc) by EOD Thu 09/20.
3) If you prefer Redwood to manage keys, we'll include that option in the quote.

Ben — can you add sandbox token pricing options to the quote and confirm whether we can enable a time-limited free sandbox for their engineers?

Sanjay — does Tue 9/21 10:00 PT work for your team?

Best,
